AGENDA
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  JULY 16, 2019
REGULAR MEETING
  5:45 PM
  NORWALK CITY HALL/COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  AND VIA VIDEOCONFERENCE

  Margarita L. Rios, Mayor
  Luigi Vernola, Vice Mayor
  Tony Ayala, Councilmember
  Jennifer Perez, Councilmember
  Leonard Shryock, Councilmember
 Public Comment: Comments may be made in person, submitted via email at: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, or through
 the video conference during the designated time on any item on the agenda or on any other matter within the jurisdiction
 subject to the rules of decorum described in Norwalk Municipal Code §2.08.020. The maximum time allowed is three
 minutes.

 Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless
 certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain
 matters for consideration at a future City Council meeting.

 Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Council:

  • Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
  • Comments should be directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

 Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City
 meeting or other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk's Department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening
 devices are available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and
 documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability.
 Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring
 that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

 Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it
 has been posted will also be made available for public inspection.

 Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City Clerk's Department, City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard
 during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday - Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every other Friday;
 telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

  STUDY SESSION MEETING – 5:00 p.m.

CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Rios

ROLL CALL
   Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FOR CLOSED SESSION MATTERS

CLOSED SESSION

  I.  PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE §54957.6; CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATOR.
  Negotiating on behalf of the City: Jesus M. Gomez, City Manager; regarding negotiations with Norwalk
  City Employees Association.

  II.  PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE §54957.6; CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATOR.
  Negotiating on behalf of the City: Jesus M. Gomez; regarding negotiations with the Norwalk
  Association of Management Employees.

  III.  CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATOR PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE
  §54956.8: Assessor Parcel Number 8045-008-902; Negotiating on behalf of the City: Jesus M. Gomez,
  City Manager; Negotiating Party: State of California; Under Negotiation: Price and Terms of Payment.

RECESS

  REGULAR MEETING – 6:00 p.m.

CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Rios

INVOCATION
  Pastor John Brito
  Spirit Life Community Church

FLAG SALUTE
  Eva Ceballos
  Norwalk High School

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

CITY COUNCIL COMMENTS

  a.  Report of City Council Travel

CITY MANAGER COMMENTS

  I.  Independence Day Celebration

  II.  Public Safety Block Party

CLOSED SESSION REPORT

CONSENT CALENDAR

Consent calendar items are considered routine matters which may be enacted by one motion and roll call vote.
Any item may be removed from the consent calendar and considered separately by City Council.

  1.  MEETING MINUTES – Staff recommends City Council approve the minutes of the meeting of July 2,
  2019. 825-04

  Minutes

  2.  PAYROLL – Staff recommends City Council approve the payroll for the period June 2, 2019 – June 15,
  2019, in the total amount of $1,183,218.56. 630
   Report

3.  COMMERCIAL DEMANDS – Staff recommends City Council approve the warrant register period June
  26, 2019 – July 9, 2019, in the total amount of $2,499,952.47. 640

  Report

4.  PLANNING COMMISSION SYNOPSIS – JULY 10, 2019 - No action is required unless the City Council
  elects to review the decision of the Planning Commission on those items where the Commission’s
  action was final. 320

  Synopsis

5.  PROJECT NO. 3302-1920 – CITYWIDE SIDEWALK/CONCRETE REPAIR AND REPLACEMENT
  MAINTENANCE PROJECT - APPROVAL OF SPECIFICATIONS AND AUTHORIZATION TO
  ADVERTISE FOR BID - Staff recommends City Council approve specifications for the
  sidewalk/concrete repair and replacement maintenance project, authorize advertisement for bids for a
  one-year term through June 30, 2020, and set a bid opening date of August 13, 2019. 1005-04-3302

  Report

6.  RESOLUTION NO. 19-45 – CHILD CARE SERVICES CONTRACTS - Staff recommends City Council:

  a.  adopt Resolution No. 19-45, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK APPROVING CHILD CARE CONTRACT AGREEMENTS WITH THE STATE
  DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION FOR FUNDING OF THE CalWORKS STAGE 2, 3 AND
  ALTERNATIVE PAYMENT CHILD CARE DEVELOPMENT PROGRAM FOR FISCAL YEAR
  2019/20; and

  b.  authorize the City Manager to execute the contracts and any amendments, provided there is
  funding in the budget, on behalf of the City, in forms approved by the City Attorney. 425-01

  Report

7.  AGREEMENT - STRATEGIC WORKFORCE PLANNING SERVICES – Staff recommends City Council
  approve Amendment No. 1 with Phillip Gallegos in the amount of $11,500 monthly from August 16,
  2019 through June 30, 2020 for strategic workforce planning services and authorize the City Manager
  to execute the amendment on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney.

  Report

8.  DELINQUENT WEED AND LITTER COLLECTION FEES – Staff recommends City Council:

  a.  confirm the attached report of the Property Maintenance and Building Rehabilitation Appeals
  Board adjusted to reflect the current outstanding balance; and

  b.  authorize the Finance Director to file a copy of this report with the County Auditor on or before
  August 10, 2019. 626-01

  Report

9.  DELINQUENT EMERGENCY BOARD-UP COLLECTION FEES - Staff recommends City Council:

  a.  confirm the attached report of the Property Maintenance and Building Rehabilitation Appeals
  Board adjusted to reflect the current outstanding balance; and

  b.  authorize the Finance Director to file a copy of this report with the County Auditor on or before
  August 10, 2019. 626-03

  Report

10. PUBLIC SAFETY COMMISSION APPROVAL OF BLUE CURB AT 12413 FIRESTONE BOULEVARD -
  No action is required unless the City Council elects to review the decision of the Public Safety
  Commission regarding approval of the blue curb. 1050-04
   Report

APPOINTMENTS

  11. ADVISORY BODIES – Staff recommends City Council make appointments to fill the vacancies on the
  various City advisory bodies. 200

  Report

  12. APPOINTMENT – NORWALK HOUSING AUTHORITY - Staff recommends City Council appoint
  LaTosha Davis to fill the remaining Tenant Commissioner term ending April 30, 2021. 315-05-01

  Report

PUBLIC HEARING

  13. DELINQUENT REFUSE COLLECTION ACCOUNTS - Staff recommends City Council approve the lien
  lists for the delinquent accounts that are not paid by July 31, 2019, and authorize staff to forward a final
  list to the Los Angeles County Tax Assessor. 626-02

  Report

REPORTS

  14. ORDINANCE NO. 19-1707 – AMENDING NORWALK MUNICIPAL CODE SUBSECTION C OF
  §12.12.340 REGARDING EXCAVATIONS IN NEW STREET IMPROVEMENTS - Staff recommends
  City Council accept for second reading and adopt Ordinance No. 19-1707. 1045

  Report

  15. CONFIRM EMERGENCY REPAIR WORK – SAN ANTONIO DRIVE – BETWEEN SPROUL STREET
  AND FIRESTONE BOULEVARD - Staff recommends City Council confirm the emergency repair work
  completed by Precision Pipeline, Inc. in the amount of $3,240.17. 955

  Report

  16. PROJECT NO. 3302-1819 – ACCEPTANCE OF WORK FOR CITYWIDE ANNUAL
  SIDEWALK/CONCRETE REPAIR AND REPLACEMENT - Staff recommends City Council accept the
  work of CJ Concrete Construction in the amount of $198,239.70 for citywide annual sidewalk/concrete
  repair and replacement. 1005-04-3302

  Report

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

ADJOURNMENT

I hereby certify under penalty of perjury under the laws of the State of California that the foregoing agenda was posted
on the City Hall bulletin board not less than 72 hours prior to the meeting. Dated July 11, 2019.

Theresa Devoy, CMC
City Clerk
